holidays.name: National Fried Rice Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble leftover-rice hero: wok-tossed, soy-sauced, and studded with egg, veggies, and whatever else is in the fridge. Grab a pan and give yesterday's rice a glamorous second act.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin, popular with takeout lovers and home cooks alike.
holidays.funFact: Fried rice is traditionally made with day-old rice because chilled, drier grains fry up fluffy instead of turning mushy.

holidays.name: National String Cheese Day
holidays.description: A salute to the snack that doubles as a toy. Peel it, pull it, and unravel it into stringy strands, because playing with your food is encouraged today.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin, celebrating the beloved lunchbox staple.
holidays.funFact: String cheese gets its stringy texture from stretching and folding the mozzarella curds, which lines up the proteins into fibers that peel apart.

holidays.name: National Pepperoni Pizza Day
holidays.description: The king of pizza toppings gets its own spotlight. Cheesy, spicy, and crowned with crispy, curled-up cups of grease, pepperoni pizza is the ultimate crowd pleaser.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin, created to honor America's favorite pizza topping.
holidays.funFact: Pepperoni is an American invention. It arose in Italian-American communities in the early 20th century, and the word comes from the Italian 'peperoni,' meaning bell peppers.
